newsitem.title: USA: Power nearly fully restored in Dakotas, Minnesota.
newsitem.headline: Power nearly fully restored in Dakotas, Minnesota.

text.p: Power outages in North Dakota dropped to just over 1,000 customers Thursday following a severe weekend snow and wind storm, utility officials said.

About 1,000 customers of Otter Tail Power Co were still without electricity in North Dakota and Minnesota early Thursday, down from about 25,000 customers without power on Sunday, a company spokesman said.

"Service has been restored to all but 11 communities. We are hopeful that we can restore all power later today," spokesman Lee Krogh said, noting 125 communities were originally affected by this weekend's storm.
Otter Tail supplies power to about 124,000 customers through eastern North Dakota, western Minnesota and northeastern South Dakota.
Northern States Power Co said electricity service has been restored to all 24,000 power customers affected by this weekend's snow and wind storm that knocked down power lines.
Northern States serves about 1.4 million customers in Minnesota, Wisconsin, North and South Dakota and Michigan.

MDU Resources Group Inc subsidiary Montana-Dakota Utilities Co had about 20 customers in Forbes, N.D., without power as of Thursday morning from outages that covered about 110,000 customers on Sunday, a company spokesman said.
Montana-Dakota Utilities, headquartered in Bismark, N.D., supplies power to customers in western North Dakota, eastern Montana and northern South Dakota.

Although temperatures are rising in North Dakota, so is the crest of the Red River. The river is expected to crest at 39.5 feet later today, which will likely pose extensive flooding threats to the area. Another system moving across the northern plains is forecast to drop more snow in the area, Weather Services Corp said.
